text: Students in the ITEs and polytechnics were also similarly subjected to higher fees in 2019.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: It is important that students from underprivileged families can enrol in IHLs to use education as a lever to uplift themselves.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: With an increasing cost of living, we hope MOE can increase the financial assistance to students in IHLs.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: I would also like to urge MOE to consider disbursing more targeted bursaries which award a different quantum, depending on the student's family income level and socio-economic background.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Mr Chairman, over the years, the Ministry has done well to ensure that our ITE adequately prepares students for careers in a knowledge-based economy.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: There are bursaries to support students in need and scholarships to affirm the good work of students.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Such programmes will be extremely beneficial for students in today's globalised interconnected world.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The question I would like to raise is whether these programmes and initiatives will also cover ITE students.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: We need to ensure that ITE students also have access and can benefit from these opportunities.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: It will serve as a form of encouragement, an eye-opener, to develop further interest in their course.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: I have met several students who were very disappointed that they could not join the CCA of their choice because they lack relevant experience.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: I am heartened to read in the news in January 2020 that MOE has started a pilot with several primary schools to remove selection trials.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: Let our children pursue sports or other interests they may have.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: CCAs should be for students to build friendships based on interest and passion.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: We should also have inter-school CCAs to encourage social mixing and bring down barriers of class.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: Inter-school CCAs can also bring together students from diverse socio-economic backgrounds and hone their interpersonal skills.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: Teachers will also have a good platform to introduce the concept of social inclusivity.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: I hope the Minister will look into my suggestion to introduce inter-school CCAs so that our students can enjoy a more enriching CCA experience.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Terence Ho, can you take both cuts together?

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Chairman, as part of holistic education, our students are exposed to arts programmes, music and aesthetics lessons.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: While there is a good range of arts programmes in schools today, they are largely ad hoc and may not be part of a longer-term vision for how the arts can play a more integral role.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: For example, there are 126 Cultural Medallion recipients, but how many of our younger generation are aware of their achievements and are inspired by their works?

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Furthermore, can MOE consider including and introducing our ethnic traditional instruments during music lessons?

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: If we do it strategically and interestingly, this could lead to the interest to participate in the school band and orchestra and provide a pipeline to build a vibrant performing arts ecosystem in the school.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Music and arts curriculum should not only be held within the classrooms.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Arts exposure at any early age continues to be important as it supports the holistic development of the child, seeds the development of future audiences while increasing the social commons.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: At the same time, an education in and through the arts helps students appreciate other cultures and develop Singapore pride.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: (In Mandarin):   Arts can stimulate curiosity and encourage creativity amongst students.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Besides the teaching of knowledge, schools are also involved in the character education and holistic development of students.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Therefore, making arts classes part of the curriculum for every student is a component of holistic education.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: When youths display talent and aptitude for the arts, we can provide more professional training platforms for them, with the hope that they will become world-class artists in the future.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: These inspirational teaching materials and personality profiles could become the cradle from which the next generation of artists can be nurtured.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: In addition, there are many artistic historical buildings in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: As the teaching of music and the arts should not be confined to the classroom, schools can consider organising field trips for students to visit these historical buildings to stimulate their interest and enhance their cultural knowledge.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Arts groups can also conduct dialogues and workshops for students to interact close up with artists.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: I would also like to suggest that MOE engage local artists and Cultural Medallion recipients during the process of curriculum planning, in order to design an arts curriculum with a stronger local flavour.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: This will help promote local arts and culture.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: We must make arts and culture accessible, and ensure that the essence of Singapore’s arts and culture is passed down from generation to generation, creating a sustainable ecosystem for the arts.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: (In English): The Arts University will serve the purpose of filling up jobs in the market contributing to the employability of these graduates.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: By transforming and upgrading our art academies, this will draw local and overseas talents into enrolling into these institutions.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Graduates from the Arts University can contribute not only to the arts and creative industry, but they are able to bring Singapore into a more competitive design and creative market in the global economy.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: From a survey, "Passion" was the most critical factor that drew workers to the arts sector; it is also the main reason why these workers remained in the sector.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Arts workers also saw themselves as contributing positively to the arts and the wider society through their work.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: For example, the Government can consider developing a research centre with the future university to grow our creative industry in the performing arts and visual art.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: These efforts will help create vibrancy in the arts scene, heighten motivation among the expected.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Why should we depend on universities in other countries to say how good our teaching is?

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Two, if we can have Singapore degrees in other subjects, why not the Arts?

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Three, the quality of the teaching and curriculum at the Nanyang Academy of Fine Arts, Lasalle and Intercultural Theatre Institute are recognised by overseas universities.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: MOE should allow a system to let Singapore academics and industry practitioners recognise the quality and approve the award of degrees.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: In recent years, there has been greater support for students with special needs in mainstream schools.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: For one, schools are equipped with allied educators who can provide more specialised support.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: There are also professional development opportunities for teachers to acquire deeper knowledge and skills in attending to students with different needs.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: There are some areas which schools could continue to work on, including helping neuro-typical students understand people with different abilities.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: This could help with normalising differences, reducing occurrences of discrimination or even bullying.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: There could also be more extensive support in transitioning students through different milestones in their educational journey by creating an ecosystem and support network with teachers, parents, therapists and people in the community.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Having well-trained staff that truly believe in the cause, is key to the quality of support for students with different needs.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Can MOE provide an update as well as more information on how it intends to equip educators in mainstream schools with the capabilities and strategies to better support students with special needs?

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: However, I believe that more can be done to ensure that all our children are given a good start in life.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: In a recent house visit, I saw two boys standing on the kitchen counter-top and another running around and their great grandmother chased him with a cane.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: The great grandparents in their late 70s are caring for three boys, age eight, nine and 10.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: The father has left the family and their mother is a Grab driver.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: She could not afford much time for them.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: The seniors told me that it has been difficult as the boys get into disciplinary issues in schools and after-school care.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: How can the UPLIFT programme identify students and families who need help?

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: Can the Minister provide an update on our UPLIFT efforts, including how MOE is strengthening after-school support and counselling support to tackle the challenges faced by disadvantaged students.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: What are the efforts to reduce long term absenteeism and drop out numbers, and have the statistics improved over the past five years?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: He shared that there were occasions where his students did not attend regular classes but would make the time to attend his soccer training sessions instead.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Ordinarily, such students would have been barred from taking part in CCA, but what was done here was different and, in my view, "uplifting".

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The teacher used the contact time during the training sessions to develop deeper relations with the students and encourage them to improve their class attendance.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Quite clearly, though, a lot of effort has to be put in to change the mindset of the students and, on some occasions, their parents too.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: What strategies have she and her colleagues identified to overcome these problems?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: How can we motivate these students to stay the course and how can the rest of the society help?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Chairman, there are many ground-up initiatives in the community to support children from underprivileged families.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: In Jurong, for example, we have stepped up our efforts over the years.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: These students are mentored by trained volunteers in the areas of life skills, social skills and leadership skills.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: If these students are underperforming in their academic studies, we will provide them with free tuition.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: We hope to share and scale this scheme.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: This is why I was excited to hear about the UPLIFT Community Pilots started by MOE.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: My experience working with the SAS recipients has shown me that it is not enough to provide financial assistance to students from disadvantaged families.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: We need to dive deep and understand the needs of the students and families, and provide necessary support like mentorship, so as to monitor, guide and to encourage the students to be the best persons they can be.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: I believe MOE's UPLIFT efforts are also in the same spirit, with the aim of providing support holistically to children and families in need.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: To do so, it is important for us to strengthen and coordinate our efforts across agencies and community partners for these students.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Moving forward, how does MOE plan to link up UPLIFT efforts with community initiatives like SAS, so that we can partner the Government to better help those students in need?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: MOE's efforts are to reduce the overemphasis on academic grades, and help students build confidence and develop a motivation to learn for life.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Education is a team effort involving not just the schools, but also parents, teachers, and the community, so that students can develop to their fullest potential.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: MOE has made many changes in recent years to work more closely with the community.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Interestingly, many of the guidelines encourage more "hands-off" parenting.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Parents are encouraged to create conducive environments and let their child develop a sense of responsibility, instead of always breaking their fall.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: If not, what else needs to be done and if yes, what positive signs have we seen?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Character building, learning to learn, becoming a better person – all these are much more challenging than scoring straight As.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: To take this forward, MOE should build strong partnerships with parents, industry partners, and the community to develop the values, dispositions and skills that will place our students in good stead for the future.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Would the Minister be able to also share details and examples of how we are working closely with our stakeholders to ensure that our students develop the right values, skills and dispositions so that they are future- ready?

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: It consists of an interrelated group of key stakeholders comprising of teachers, schools, parents and the wider community, so that together they strive to allow our students to develop holistically to their fullest potential.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: I am heartened that MOE has made many good changes in recent years to work more closely with the community and to build stronger partnerships.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Mr Chairman, Sir, let me start with Ms Denise Phua's question.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Ms Phua asked if MOE has a transformation map.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Two years ago, we launched something like that.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We launched a reform movement of the education system and we called it "Learn for Life".

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But Members are probably not very familiar with it because we did not launch everything we want to do with a big bang, so no big headlines.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Instead, we paced out the announcement of each thrust of the movement, adopted multi-year implementation plans, so that schools, parents and students can fully understand the changes and can adapt to these.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: One, I will give a short update on what we have done so far.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Two, I will talk about the new things we are doing – yes, we are doing some new things.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We have rolled out four thrusts to improve the system we have today.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The first is nurturing the "Joy of Learning".

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Mr Murali Pillai and Mr Lim Biow Chuan have asked for an update on this.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Joy of learning does not mean schools should be just all fun and games.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Joy comes from purposeful learning, from a sense of progress and fulfilment by doing something challenging, hard and meaningful.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Then, you feel a sense of accomplishment and you get joy from that.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We hope this will change the psychology of students and parents towards PSLE and reduce the over-emphasis on academic results.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The new scoring system, its biggest impact, actually, is that it will affect Secondary school postings and parents are naturally anxious.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We will help students and parents familiarise themselves with this new system.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This will be based on last year’s Secondary One Posting Exercise and PSLE results.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Next year, we will release another set of simulated cut-off points based on this year’s Secondary One Posting Exercise results.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, two sets of simulated cut-off points before the system goes live in 2021.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It is not that these are definite cut-off points.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: There can be changes from year to year, as choice patterns change.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: And when the system goes "live", cut-off-points can change further.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Notwithstanding this, we hope that by giving parents information early, we can better support them in making Secondary school choices for their children.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Another major move is the reduction of school-based exams.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: By next year, it will be 100% based on our implementation schedule.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: By next year, it will be 100% too.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Some schools, such as the School of Science and Technology (SST), have removed mid-year exams for Secondary 1 to 3 in one shot.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: When I visited the school, the students I spoke to were very happy with the change.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They said with the time freed up, they can now do interesting hands-on stuff like coding, designing robots, making prototypes and so on.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: With more freed up time, other schools such as Gan Eng Seng Secondary introduced a programme called the Learning Fortnight.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They do projects, learn a new sport, attend enrichment activities, and enjoy them.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: However, in general – I will be honest – I think the responses have been varied.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: When I speak with Primary school students, most will say, "Hooray, fewer exams", so they are very happy.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But many Secondary school students told me they are not happy; they prefer to have mid-year exams.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It may surprise you but it is true.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They say, "Now, without the mid-year exams, we have all these continuous mini-assessments throughout the year.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: That is more stressful!" So, I told these students that they have gotten used to exams, which is why we have to change.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: On the other hand, Primary school students, their learning habits have yet to be formed and, therefore, they welcome the change.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, I advised the Secondary students that these exams are really part and parcel of learning, and they are really not high-stakes.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The mini-assessment is not going to affect your future – not very likely.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, focus on learning throughout the year, rather than cram your studies and "mug" just before exams; that is a less effective learning habit.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Along the way, seek your teachers’ help when necessary and schools will do their best to help you progress.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: As Mr Lim Biow Chuan pointed out, many students and parents have deep-seated mindsets about exams – not easy to change.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But we are trying to change the paradigm.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, instead of tests and exams, the desire and joy of learning should be at the centre of school life.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Indeed, as the Member has said, the stakes of exams are high actually because of admission into the next level of education – from PSLE to Secondary school, Secondary school to Polytechnic or Junior College (JC).

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: That is why MOE has been very active in reviewing admission systems across levels.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We reviewed the Direct School Admission (DSA) system for Secondary school students.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We introduced aptitude-based admission systems for our Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs).

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We have done that; the Polytechnics went first.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Right now, the Universities are doing it with great rigour.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The different admission systems are still being refined to reduce the over-emphasis on exam results, and more changes will come in the coming years.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Now, the second thrust of "Learn for Life" is "One Secondary Education, Many Subject Bands".

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Mr Charles Chong and Mr Murali Pillai have asked for an update.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Number one, allowing lower Secondary Normal stream students to take Humanities subjects at a more demanding level.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The second change is more interesting – which is that schools are re-organising form classes so that they comprise students from different streams.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The form classes take some subjects together, such as Art, PE, CCE and Design & Technology.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: For other subjects, students will split up into different classes based on their subject bands.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Of course, we designed all these before COVID-19 but now we have a situation to manage.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Some schools have organised the form classes by CCAs, others by their "House" systems.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Most schools just like Deyi Secondary School, placed students in classes to ensure a good balance of stream, gender, race as well as learning needs.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Deyi Secondary held an orientation camp for the Secondary 1 students to get to know one another.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The teachers told me that during the camp, they made a point not to look at the background of the students.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They did not know what stream the students were from during the camp, so that there would be no pre-conceived notions.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They observed the students, identified those with leadership skills and initiative, and after the camp was all over, they appointed them as class leaders.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: After that, they opened the file and looked at the background of the students.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: To their great delight, the leaders comprised students from Express, Normal (Academic), and Normal (Technical) streams as well.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The character of the students shone through regardless of their streams.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Another teacher at Deyi reflected how Full SBB is changing his subconscious mindset.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: He proceeded to stop the student and asked the three standard questions that he would pose in such a situation.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Second question: “What level are you?” The child said, “Secondary 1, teacher.” Then, he asked the third question: “Which class are you from?” And Bono said, "1-Determination." Then, the teacher got stumped.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Because in the past, if you know the class, you know the stream of the child.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: He did not know what stream the child is from.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: And then he realised all this while, his line of questioning in such a disciplinary situation was to find out the stream of the child.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: He reflected to himself: why is that relevant?

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This is not about whether an Express, Normal (Academic) or Normal (Technical) student has broken a school rule.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Bono needs a haircut – that is all.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It is possible that some of us may well have this subconscious mindset.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But this teacher was really wise, brave and honest to be aware of it, and to acknowledge it.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The third thrust is "Education as an Uplifting Force".

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Inequality is an issue every society has to grapple with and education is the best social leveller.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We are doing a lot more to tackle inequality through education, including investing significantly in pre-school education, setting up more student care centres, enhancing bursary schemes, implementing targeted programmes that bring social partners and community partners together.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Second Minister Indranee will speak more about this later.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: With a good foundation, almost all our students today progress to post-Secondary institutions today.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Seventy percent – the large majority – goes to Polytechnics or Autonomous Universities.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Mr Ang Wei Neng was worried about affordability of course fees for the lower income group.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: If that is still too much, he can take up a tuition loan.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: When they graduate, 90% of them who want to join the labour force find work within six months; that is our track record.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: By the time they step into the workforce, they would have more or less pressed a reset button that mitigated their childhood disadvantages.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This is uplift in action, where all young Singaporeans can access opportunities, because we have a stable country, a growing economy and a good education system.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The fourth thrust is "Learning Languages for Life".

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Ms Tin Pei Ling and Mr Lim Biow Chuan asked about MOE’s bilingualism effort.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The Member lamented that he only realised the importance of Mother Tongue Language (MTL) in adulthood, after he stepped into his professional life.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Unfortunately, some things do not change, and I think many of our students will still feel the same way as Mr Lim when they grow up.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Hence, it is critical to start as young as possible and make students interested in learning MTL.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This requires schools and families to complement each other's efforts.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Families can provide an immersive MTL environment at home.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Then, schools carry on the work, starting with kindergartens putting stronger emphasis on the teaching of MTLs in pre-schools, which we have started to do.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The Programme supports students to attain a higher level of MTL proficiency and acquire a better understanding of their culture.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: About 250 students took it up, which is an encouraging start.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It also helps to have specialised schools, like the Special Assistance Plan (SAP) schools and programmes like the Elective Programme in Malay Language for Secondary Schools (EMAS) and the National Elective Tamil Language Programme (NETP).

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: In other words, let us not shy away from doing what it takes to preserve the use of MTLs.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The world is moving towards bilingualism, even multilingualism.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We have an advantage because of our ethnic diversity and bilingual abilities.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We must not only preserve this advantage, but strengthen it further.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They have to do with curriculum – what we teach and how we teach.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We need to refresh our curriculum to evolve with the needs and realities of the times.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But any changes to curriculum must be very carefully considered.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It shapes the values, attitudes, mindsets and competencies of an entire generation.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It gives meaning to MOE's mission of "moulding the future of the nation".

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: For example, we introduced Values-in-Action (VIA) in 2012 to foster social responsibility amongst young Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Today, you can see its imprint in our young Singaporeans, in the way they look at social issues.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: As Dr Intan and Mr Ang Wei Neng pointed out, events like the COVID-19 outbreak also offer a valuable opportunity in education.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Schools today are placing strong emphasis on personal hygiene and on social responsibility.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: If we keep all these practices up, even after the crisis has blown over, I think we will have a generation of Singaporeans who will be much more resilient to infectious diseases.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Today we face new challenges and realities that necessitate a refreshing of our curriculum.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They are in three areas: first, in Character and Citizenship Education (CCE); second, Knowing Asia; third, Digital Literacy.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: There are a few components to our CCE today, such as the teaching of values, National Education, Social and Emotional Learning, and Education and Career Guidance.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: In 2016, we started a comprehensive review of the CCE curriculum.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The more we progressed in the review, the more we thought it in urgent need of change.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Because the young today are different from previous generations in one major aspect, which is their exposure to technology.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: For those who follow comics and watch superhero movies, they are like Bruce Wayne, who is also Batman – one day, one night.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They have one real world that parents can see and another one online, which they spend a lot of time on, that parents do not see.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: As adults who have grown up without this duality and without this space, I do not think we fully understand what our young are going through.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The impact of technology on students and on children is complex and multi-faceted.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But let me just highlight one of the most significant effects, which is that technology presents children with the influences, choices and decisions previous generations never had to contend with.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: In an online world, you can be anonymous and there are no policemen, no editors, no verifiers.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: A child can choose to be nasty and then get away with it.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Whereas in the real world, it is not easy to say something nasty to your friend in the face; a punch can come back.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: In fact, sometimes there is nothing very social about social media.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: More importantly now, with a powerful device in their hands, our children can decide: do I use it to acquire knowledge for learning, or access undesirable materials?

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Do I use it to keep in touch with family and friends, or get addicted to digital entertainment?

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Do I use it to record beautiful memories, take pictures with my friends or intrude into the privacy of others, or worse, commit a sexual offence?

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: How do we ensure that our young make the right choices and survive well in an online world?

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I think digital world problems require analogue world solutions.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It goes back to our values, our morals, our humanity.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Values are what distinguish us from computers and machines, and that we cannot abdicate to technology.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We apply our moral and values system whether we are offline or we are online.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We determine the purpose of technology, we determine the purpose of devices.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Dr Intan said that values are more often caught than taught.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Families play a big part in instilling them in the young, at home.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But schools can then work with parents and make a big difference too.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Today, CCE lessons cover both character and values, and also citizenship.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: For Primary 1 to 3, we will henceforth devote the bulk of CCE lessons to character and values.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: As the Chinese saying goes, "品德在先，学术在后" – values before academics.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We will emphasise respect and care for others, honesty, humility and kindness.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Our children need to learn to stand up against discrimination, against bullying – of all kinds and regardless of who the victim is.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Many of these lessons will be taught in MTL from Primary 1 to 6.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We will therefore better align the CCE and MTL lessons – ensure that the standard of the language is appropriate and engage students in much more interesting ways.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: From Primary 4 to 6, we will broaden the existing Form Teacher Guidance Period to include National Education and citizenship topics – values relevant to us as a nation.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: For these topics, it is more meaningful to have a diverse group of students from all communities and therefore, these classes will continue to be taught in English.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We will devote more time and develop more materials to teach this subject, so that students will learn to critically evaluate what they read online, be able to tell genuine news from falsehoods and not rely on social media "likes" for validation.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They need to be able to say no to bad influences, and protect themselves from cyber bullies and predators.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Several Secondary schools – in fact, 11 – have piloted the new CCE curriculum on cyber wellness.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I visited one of them – New Town Secondary – and observed a class on the topic of cyber bullying.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This was conducted via a video case study and students were asked at every juncture of the story to vote and decide how the story would unfold.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, they could tell how their decisions affected the outcome of the story.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I could tell the situation resonated with them and the students were very engaged.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: To me, the lesson that day was quite clear.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The lesson is: if you encounter cyber bullying, seek help and support, do not retaliate.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: That day, the students voted for retaliation, even though I was sitting there!

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: And the ending did not turn out well.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This is one way we are using more authentic scenarios, immersive modalities and giving students more voice and agency to bring CCE to life – not just for cyber wellness, but for all aspects of CCE.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The new CCE curriculum will seek to strengthen one important aspect, which is peer support.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Second Minister Indranee will speak more on this topic.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Fourth, we will expand our efforts to engage secondary school students more actively on contemporary issues through CCE lessons.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We will explore more topics, find ways to engage students more deeply and increase the frequency of these lessons to at least once a fortnight.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Climate change, as Miss Cheng Li Hui and Mr Yee Chia Hsing suggested, could be one of these issues.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Other examples could be Government policies, social inequality, race and religion, online falsehoods and so on and so forth.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Mr Leon Perera suggested including a subject like Theory of Knowledge (TOK) into our school curriculum.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: MOE is quite reluctant to over-crowd our curriculum.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It is already quite a heavy curriculum, especially given that TOK is a pre-university subject for the International Baccalaureate Diploma Programme.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Some of these contemporary issues and the discussion of them will help hone the critical thinking skills of our students.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They may be sensitive to discuss, but they are important to help our students better understand the complexities of our country and our life.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Teachers will guide students to listen attentively, converse respectfully and be open to differing perspectives.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We will have to, as Miss Cheng Li Hui suggested, further integrate CCE into school lessons and activities, such as CCAs, camps, learning journeys and Values-in-Action.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: With these changes, every school experience can be a CCE lesson.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: And every school a good school, of course.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This is happening in some schools, but we will implement it system-wide, be more deliberate about CCE and make learning intentional rather than incidental.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The second area of curriculum review is Knowing Asia.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Several Members, such as Ms Foo Mee Har, Mr Murali Pillai and Mr Teo Ser Luck, have explained why this is important.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Suffice to say that Southeast Asia is one of the fastest growing regions in the world.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Together with China, India, Japan and Korea, they all form part of our natural hinterland.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Singapore-based enterprises need to be able to venture out to the region.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: And Singaporeans must be able to play a part in it.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: To do so, we need to be equipped with the relevant knowledge, language and cultural skills.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But, like all skills, it takes many years, even decades of experience, to become a country or a regional expert.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: What the education system can do, is to get our students started young and expose them to the region.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We will give the study of Asia its due emphasis in Humanities subjects.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: For example, in history, students will learn more about the Vietnam War and how developments in Southeast Asia is intertwined with the complexity of the Cold War.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: In Social Studies, students can learn about the importance of ASEAN centrality.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Overseas trips have taken a backseat due to COVID-19 but I am sure, in time, the crisis will blow over.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The younger ones in schools attend student exchanges, cultural enrichment or embark on service learning projects.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The older ones in IHLs typically go for overseas internships and immersion programmes in a foreign education institution.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: These have been effective in building their cross-cultural skills, resourcefulness and resilience.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Students generally enjoy overseas trips, but I think their favourite destinations are still New York and London.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We will organise more trips to Asian countries and encourage students to participate in them.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Students from the West are flocking here to experience Asia because of the cultural diversity and the exciting economic opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This is our own backyard and, here, we will always have a natural competitive advantage.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We will need that mindset shift that Mr Teo Ser Luck talked about.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, it is not an exclusive experience, as Mr Faisal Manap puts it.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Third, we can know our region better through the learning of languages.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: A good start is to learn our Mother Tongue Languages (MTLs) better.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Where possible – I keep coming back to learning MTL better – and if the students have the aptitude and interest, we will also encourage the learning of third languages.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: For most students, this will be at a conversational level and it is not examinable.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, to Mr Chen Show Mao’s suggestion – I know the Member has been raising this every year – that MOE make the learning of conversational Malay compulsory in Primary school, I think it is better that we continue to emphasise the learning of a student’s own MTL.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: As it is, many students are already finding that quite challenging.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But we have been encouraging students to learn the language of another community at a conversational level.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We are encouraging more schools to do so and more schools will do so.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: There is also value for our young to learn to converse in regional languages, as Members have suggested.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We will pair the learning of conversational ASEAN languages with overseas school trips.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: That way, learning is more meaningful and can be immediately applied and more students can access it.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The third area of curriculum review is digital literacy.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Ms Denise Phua, Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar, Miss Cheng Li Hui and Mr Ang Wei Neng spoke about this.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We all know how digital literacy is important for our young.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: One popular response around the world is "Let us make coding compulsory in schools!" But that is too simplistic.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Not everyone will grow up to be a coder.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Many of us just need to learn how to use technology and software and be comfortable with using them.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Further, programming languages will become outdated by the time the students graduate.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Another popular response is, "Let us give every student a digital device".

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It is not a bad idea, but it can do more harm than good if the device becomes another gadget that is a big distraction for the student.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, if we want to do this, we must do it in the right sequence – make sure that the curriculum is rightly designed, teachers are equipped with the suitable pedagogical skills, then use the device to enhance teaching and learning.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We need to think about digital literacy more deeply and holistically, rather than simply implementing immediate things that come to mind.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: One way is to think of digital literacy like language literacy.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: First, both are generative or seminal skills, allowing a learner, after you have learnt it, to access knowledge in other domains.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We do not teach children language just through the formal lessons, but within a holistic and immersive environment.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Likewise, we should embed digital literacy within our overall school curriculum and not as a standalone subject.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Third, we can break digital literacy into productive and receptive components – listen and speak, read and write.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: In Chinese – 听，说，读，写。 We are conscious of how we teach each of these components, how they relate to each other and how they reinforce each other.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We, too, can break digital literacy down into different components.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They represent the different and mutually-reinforcing aspects of digital literacy.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This is MOE’s contribution to the national effort, with a focus on schools and IHLs.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It means being able to gather and use information and data from digital resources.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Our young have no problem doing that; they are digital natives.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Their challenge is how to do it in a constructive, safe, responsible and ethical way.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This will be taught through the cyber wellness component of the new CCE curriculum that I spoke about earlier.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This is the ability to manage, analyse, interpret and understand data and then solve problems systematically.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: What schools can do is to explicitly draw out the learning points from Mathematics.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Let us take an example – the teaching of prime numbers.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I hope Members remember what prime numbers are.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: A prime number is one that is not divisible by any other number.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Today, teachers typically explain the process to identify prime numbers as follows: for a set of numbers, say one to 100, cross out one, then the teacher will say, "Then, all the higher multiples of 2, cancel off; then all the higher multiples of 3, cancel off; we skip 4 because it is divisible by 2; and then we go to 5, you skip 6 and go 7 and, finally, what you are left with are prime numbers." All of us went through that, right?

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: In future, to be more explicit about developing computational thinking, teachers can challenge students to write a simple program to follow that same logical sequence.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Through such an exercise, students learn various programming structures, such as loops and conditions.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: One common programming logic is: "if, then, else".

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, applied to this example, if a number is a multiple of 2, then you take it out, it is not a prime number, or else you retain it as a possible prime number and you loop back and you try with 3 and then 5, 7 and so on.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: With this, the already renowned Singapore Mathematics curriculum has received another upgrade!

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We need to teach students to use software and devices productively to learn to work for daily living across different contexts.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: To Mr Chen Show Mao's question, we started building it a few years ago, way before there was COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The idea is not to make students learn completely online and not have to go to school.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The quality and outcomes of e-learning will never be the same as a physical learning environment with teachers, friends, CCAs and a social setting.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Neither are we using SLS to make the classroom high-tech and futuristic.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: What we want to do is to use SLS to enhance the classroom experience.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Let the technology fade into the background, and let the interaction, thinking and discussion come to the fore.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Flip the classroom, give students more voice, make learning become collaborative.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They are nothing like the lessons that I went through as a kid.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: At Orchid Park Secondary, I saw how a Mathematics teacher, Mr Marwin Low, used SLS to teach students about angles within a diagram.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, after the students logged on to SLS, they were shown a quadrilateral on screen.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The students could drag each of the corners and change the shape and size of the quadrilateral.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But no matter how they manipulated the diagram, a display at the side will show that the addition of all the interior angles was always 360 degrees.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The concept is presented visually and it is very clear.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They were then presented with various tasks, which they had to solve and use SLS to key in their answers.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Students can remain anonymous and give themselves nicknames.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They could also see each other's answers, comment on them or pose questions.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: In this online space, anonymity is put to good use as the students experience a much higher level of psychological safety in learning, as Prof Lim Sun Sun puts it.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The teacher could monitor the answer given by every student in real-time, through a heat map.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: If the heat map is filled with green dots, it means everyone got the answer right and the lesson carries on.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: If it is all red dots, it means everyone has got it wrong, and the teacher had better re-teach the concept.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: If it is mostly green with some red dots, it means that some students need coaching and the teacher will know who they are and can intervene accordingly.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: At last year’s Malay Language Anugerah Arif Budiman Teachers’ Award, one of the winners was Cikgu Siti Mariam from Crest Secondary.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I asked her how she managed to make her MTL lesson interesting and engaging.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: In her case, she incorporated her students' interest in photography into the lesson.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The students would take photos using their mobile devices, prepare a photo story in Malay and then upload it on an online platform and share it with the rest of their classmates.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: There are many ground-up digital lesson plans that teachers have created and uploaded onto the SLS platform to share with their colleagues.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, we are now crowd-sourcing digital lesson plans.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: And I think we are still just scratching the surface of this very powerful SLS tool.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: A second important insight from this pilot is that to conduct e-learning, it is very useful for every student to have a personal learning device.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: A device is as essential for e-learning in a digital learning classroom, just as paper and pen are for a traditional classroom.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: A third lesson is that having issued a device to every student, there has to be controlled access so that the device is used for education and learning and not other distractions.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The pilot schools have effectively addressed this through device usage control.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It can access educationally meaningful sites on the Internet, but online games and Korean dramas are out.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It will also monitor students’ use of the device and where they have gone to.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Some students are naturally disappointed with the limited functionality of their devices, but it is a necessary thing to do.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It is consistent with a common school practice where mobile phone usage is disallowed during school hours.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We are now ready to expand the pilot programme.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Over the next few years, MOE will progressively roll out this new way of teaching nation-wide, to all Secondary schools.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This could be a tablet, a laptop or a chromebook.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We will make sure that the device is affordable.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Given that it is primarily used for learning and education, we do not intend for it to be a high-end device.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We will use a bulk tender to lower the price further, probably, I think, to a few hundred dollars.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Students can pay for the device through their Edusave accounts.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Last year, we raised the Government's annual contribution to the Edusave accounts.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We expect most students to have enough balance in their Edusave accounts to pay for the device.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The last component of the digital literacy framework is "Create".

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It is the productive mode, that is, the ability to code a programme, develop an app, create a website, design a game and collaborate with others in the process.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Many Secondary schools are leveraging Applied Learning Programmes to get students to develop software or programme robots.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We will also expand the number of schools offering "O" Level computing, from 22 to 30 schools; and "A" Level computing from eight Junior Colleges (JCs) to 10 JCs.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: To Ms Denise Phua's question, MOE has also partnered the Special Education (SPED) schools to customise digital literacy to the learning needs of their students.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: For example, Pathlight School offers "O" Level computing.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: For home-schoolers, they can refer to materials that MOE has made available to the public.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Mr Ang Wei Neng asked about the efforts at IHLs in pushing digital literacy.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: IHLs are setting baseline digital competency requirements for all their students.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: For example, at SMU, students take a module on Introductory Statistics.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: At Nanyang Polytechnic (NYP), computational thinking is a compulsory Year 1 foundational module.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The IHLs are also upgrading their curriculum for sectors that require more advanced digital skills, such as cybersecurity, finance, manufacturing and logistics.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: In the last three years, the Autonomous Universities (AUs) have trained about 1,000 ICT graduates annually.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But the AUs know that the industry is hungry for more talent and have been working very hard to expand the capacity of ICT courses.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: And we will find ways to ramp up the capacity further if need be.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I have spoken about many changes in the education system.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The most important common success factor for all the changes we are making is our teachers.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I think we have the best teaching force in the world to make our education reforms a success.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Over the years, we have been able to recruit very good teachers.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Many are attracted to the noble mission of education, in helping to mould the future of our nation.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Having recruited teachers, we then need to continue to invest in their professional competencies, a point alluded to by Mr Murali Pillai and Miss Cheng Li Hui.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, MOE surveyed our teachers and asked them, given the changing education landscape, what kind of skills do you need most?

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, they provided their inputs and the following are the six competencies that teachers told us they needed.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: As we reduce exam load, teachers want to be able to use other assessment tools, such as project work, quizzes and class presentations.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They want to be able to design and conduct a class that encourages active learning, giving students more time to explore, pose questions and find answers.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Three, differentiated instruction, so that in more diverse classrooms, teachers can teach in a way that caters to the different strengths and learning needs of the students.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Four, support for students with special educational needs.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: About 80% of our students with special educational needs (SEN) are in our mainstream schools today.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Teachers want to have a better understanding of their needs and support them better.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Five, e-pedagogy, so that they can use digital technology effectively to enhance learning and especially with the NDLP.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Some may ask: how will older teachers keep up with all these new demands in education?

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I think it is a misperception that older teachers, and for that matter, older workers, cannot keep up with changes.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Senior Minister of State Chee Hong Tat was a guest-of-honour at the Distinguished Chinese Language Teacher Awards Ceremony last year.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The most experienced award recipient was Mdm Lee Pick Siew.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: She has taught Chinese for 24 years at St Joseph's Institution (SJI).

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Senior Minister of State Chee spoke to her about education technology.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: And that is coming from the most senior teacher that evening.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Others are concerned that with professional development, teachers will have one more thing to worry about, on top of their teaching and administrative duties.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Teachers have been doing it for many years.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Our teachers were very forthcoming with their input because they want to learn, be good at what they are doing and grow in their careers.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It is essential in determining the standards of practice, developing mastery, deepening capabilities and instilling professional pride.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: If you cannot do that, you are like a chef who just reheats the food that somebody else cooked.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Mr Chairman, Sir, let me conclude and summarise the key thrusts of our reform efforts.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: As you can tell, it is a MOE designed handout.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: It is what Second Minister Indranee calls, the "Tree for Life".

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: At the very base, the ground, it represents our mission which is UPLIFT, making sure that every child has opportunities.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: No child is left behind because of their family backgrounds.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And then, the leaves and the fruits represent what we are populating the classroom with, which is refreshing our curriculum to prepare our students to be future-ready – in CCE, Knowing Asia and Digital Literacy.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The sun represents what is critical for the system to work well – our teachers.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And through SkillsFuture for Educators, we are upgrading their skills and professionalism.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I hope this is the transformation map Ms Denise Phua is asking for.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I hope it lives up to her expectation.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I hope it is as thoughtful as it is bold.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The constant improvement of our public systems, like education, is a core aspect of our governance approach and our social compact.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Technology and globalisation – yes, they bring about great opportunities, but they can also aggravate inequality and stifle social mobility.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: When I visited Orchid Park Secondary, one of our pilot schools to implement the use of personal learning devices, I met a Chemistry teacher.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: He said something that left a very deep impression.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: He said that the most profound implication of the initiative is not the technology or the new pedagogy.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: It is that now, every student is similarly equipped in terms of computer resources and learning resources.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And then, with the SLS, he readily hears the voice of every child in class.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The teacher can now more easily detect and zoom in to the students who have somehow fallen behind.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: In other words, this initiative has further levelled the playing field for all students.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And that is the most significant outcome of this programme.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And that is also the objective of MOE's other initiatives rolled out over the years, whether it is Applied Learning Programme, Values-In-Action, Outdoor Adventure Learning, Language Elective Programme or the Junior Sports Academy.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We are always improving the common experiences of our students.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: In many countries, social stratification worsened partly because the national system deteriorated.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, the affluent opt out of the national system and they pay for market-based solutions.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Over time, this further entrenched the gap between the rich and the poor, who live in worlds far apart – stratification worsens.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We will make sure no one is denied a good education because of their family background.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Within these commons, we enable social mobility, we help children from poor families break out of poverty, we build a platform for all Singaporeans to mingle and build bonds.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We can fulfil the aspirations and dreams of successive generations.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: From Learn for Life to SkillsFuture, we will inculcate the spirit of lifelong learning in our young and ensure that they will be ready for the future.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Chairman, the Government is committed to nurturing every Singaporean to their fullest potential.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Minister Ong has just shown you our roadmap through the "Tree for Life".

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: But even as we transform the education system to help Singaporeans seize opportunities of the future, we will ensure that education remains an uplifting force that provides opportunities for all, regardless of their background or the challenges they face.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: One key challenge our youths face today is mental well-being.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Prof Lim Sun Sun spoke about the importance of building positive learning environments; Ms Rahayu Mahzam and Assoc Prof Daniel Goh suggested strengthening mental health education in schools, to equip our students to handle life’s challenges; while Ms Anthea Ong asked if we can increase the number of counsellors and introduce mental health screenings.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Student well-being is of utmost importance to MOE.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Our efforts in this area are guided by three broad questions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: First, at the most basic level, how can we create a positive learning environment in our schools?

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Second, how can we equip our students with the knowledge and skills they need to overcome challenges and setbacks?

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: And finally, how can we support the small group of students with more serious mental health challenges?

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: So, let me address each of these in turn.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: First, creating a positive school learning environment for all students.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Our teachers and school leaders play a crucial role in this.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In our Singapore Teaching Practice (STP) model, creating a "positive classroom culture" is a fundamental teaching process.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The STP is covered in pre-service training at NIE, as well as in-service courses by the Academy of Singapore Teachers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In CCE, positive teacher-student relationships are strongly emphasised.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We will also be developing our teachers’ competencies in establishing strong teacher-student relationships, and providing a caring and enabling environment, through the CCE practice area of SkillsFuture for Educators.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As Prof Lim Sun Sun acknowledged, the vast majority of our teachers undertake their roles with professionalism and care.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Having laid the foundation of a positive school learning environment, the next step is to build resilience, by equipping our students with the skills and knowledge to overcome setbacks.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: And, "I can" emphasises skills that will enable students to cope and thrive, including emotion regulation, problem-solving and managing relationships and conflicts. "I have", which is about tapping on support, including peer support, can be really powerful in schools.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Research has shown that having a sense of affiliation among peers, positive vibes and feeling supported by one another, all contribute to positive well-being.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Some of our schools have already introduced peer support structures, to good effect.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: To illustrate, let me share an example from Bukit Merah Secondary School.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We have changed the students’ names to protect their privacy.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
